9026.text: The locus of a variable point whose chord of contact w.r.t. the hyperbola $\dfrac{x2}{a2} - \dfrac{y2}{b2} =1$ subtends a right angle at the origin is
9026.sol:
Given,

The equation of the given hyperbola is& $\dfrac{x2}{a2} - \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1 ⋯ \left(1\right)$

Now let $\left(h, k\right)$ be the pole of a chord& $PQ$ of the hyperbola

Then the straight line& $PQ$ is the polar of the point& $\left(h, k\right)$ w.r.t. the hyperbola and so its equation is

$\dfrac{xh}{a2} - \dfrac{yk}{b2} =1 ⋯ \left(2\right)$

Now the center of the hyperbola is the origin, let it be point $C$,

Now making& $\left(1\right)$ homogeneous with the help of& $\left(2\right)$, the combined equation of& $CP$ and& $CQ$ is

$\dfrac{x2}{a2} - \dfrac{y2}{b2} =\left(\dfrac{xh}{a2} - \dfrac{yk}{b2}\right)2 ⋯ \left(3\right)$

Now the chord $PQ$ subtends a right angle at& $\left(0, 0\right)$

Therefore the lines $CP$ and& $CQ$ given by& $\left(3\right)$ are perpendicular and so in the equation& $\left(3\right)$, we have the coefficient of $x^{2} +$coefficient of $y^{2} = 0$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{1}{a2} - \dfrac{h2}{a4}\right) + \left(\dfrac{- 1}{b2} - \dfrac{k2}{b4}\right) =0$

$⇒ \dfrac{h2}{a4} + \dfrac{k2}{b4} = \dfrac{1}{a2} - \dfrac{1}{b2}$

Thus locus is

$\dfrac{x2}{a4} + \dfrac{y2}{b4} = \dfrac{1}{a2} - \dfrac{1}{b2}$

9302.text: If $\dfrac{x4}{( x - 1 ) ( x - 2 )} =$ f ( x ) + $\dfrac{A}{x - 1} + \dfrac{B}{x - 2}, then $
9302.sol:
Given $\dfrac{{x}^{4}}{( x - 1 ) ( x - 2 )} = f ( x ) + \dfrac{A}{x - 1} + \dfrac{B}{x - 2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{x}^{4}}{( x - 1 ) ( x - 2 )} = \dfrac{f ( x ) \left(x - 1\right)\left(x - 2\right) + A\left(x - 2\right) + B\left(x - 1\right)}{\left(x - 1\right)\left(x - 2\right)}$

$⇒ {x}^{4} = f ( x ) \left(x - 1\right)\left(x - 2\right) + A\left(x - 2\right) + B\left(x - 1\right)$

On putting $x = 1$, we get $A = - 1$

On putting $x = 2$, we get $B = 16$

Then, ${x}^{4} = f ( x ) \left(x - 1\right)\left(x - 2\right) - \left(x - 2\right) + 16\left(x - 1\right)$

$⇒ {x}^{4} - 16x + 16 + x - 2 = f ( x ) \left(x - 1\right)\left(x - 2\right)$

$⇒ f ( x ) = \dfrac{{x}^{4} - 15x + 14}{\left(x - 1\right)\left(x - 2\right)}$

On adding and Subtracting ${x}^{2}$, we get

$f ( x ) = \dfrac{{x}^{4} - 15x + 14 + {x}^{2} - {x}^{2}}{\left(x - 1\right)\left(x - 2\right)} = \dfrac{\left({x}^{4} - {x}^{2} - 12x + 12\right) + \left({x}^{2} - 3x + 2\right)}{\left({x}^{2} - 3x + 2\right)}$

$⇒ f ( x ) = \dfrac{\left({x}^{4} - {x}^{2} - 12x + 12\right)}{\left({x}^{2} - 3x + 2\right)} + 1$

$⇒ f ( x ) = \dfrac{\left(x - 1\right)\left({x}^{3} + {x}^{2} - 12\right)}{\left(x - 1\right)\left(x - 2\right)} + 1$

$⇒ f ( x ) = \dfrac{{x}^{3} + {x}^{2} + x - 14}{x - 2}$

$⇒ f ( x ) = {x}^{2} + 3x + 7$

9694.subject: Mathematics
9694.sol:
Let \(P=\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{n}[(n+1)(n+2) \ldots \ldots(2 n)]^{1 / n}\)
On applying ' \(\log ^{\prime}\) both sides, we get
\(\log P=\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{n} \left[\log \left(\frac{n+1}{n}\right)\left(\frac{n+2}{n}\right) \ldots \ldots\left(\frac{n+n}{n}\right)\right]\)
\(\begin{aligned}
 =\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{n} \sum_{r=1}^ n \log \lleft(1+\frac{r}{n}\right)=\int_0^1 \log (1+x) d x \\
& =[x \log (1+x)]_0^1-\int_0^1 \frac{x}{1+x}d x \\
& =\log 2-(x-\log (1+x))_0^1 \\
& =\log 2-1+\log 2 \\
& =\log 4-1=\log \left(\frac{4}{e}\right) \RightarrowP=\frac{4}{e}
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, option (d) is correct.

11087.text: In a triangle $ABC$, if $3sinA + 4cosB = 6$ and $4sinB + 3cosA = 1$, then $sin ( A + B )$ is equal to
11087.sol:
Given,& $3sinA + 4cosB = 6$~and $4sinB + 3cosA = 1$

On squaring and adding both the equations we get,

$\left(3sinA + 4cosB\right)2 + \left(4sinB + 3cosA\right)2 = {6}^{2} + {1}^{2}$

$⇒ 9{sin}^{2}A + 16{cos}^{2}B + 24sinAcosB + 16{sin}^{2}B + 9{cos}^{2}A + 24sinBcosA = 37$

$⇒ 9\left({sin}^{2}A + {cos}^{2}A\right) + 16\left({cos}^{2}B + {sin}^{2}B\right) + 24\left(sinAcosB + sinBcosA\right) = 37$

Using~${sin}^{2}A + {cos}^{2}A = 1$~and& $sin ( A + B ) = sinAcosB + cosAsinB$

$⇒ 9 + 16 + 24sin\left(A + B\right) = 37$

$⇒ 24sin\left(A + B\right) = 37 - 25 = 12$

$⇒ sin ( A + B ) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

11263.text: If $\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \alpha_3, \alpha_4, \alpha_5$ are the roots of $x^5-5 x^4+9 x^3-9 x^2+5 x-1=0$ then $\frac{1}{\alpha_1^2}+\frac{1}{\alpha_2^2}+\frac{1}{\alpha_3^2}+\frac{1}{\alpha_4^2}+\frac{1}{\alpha_5^2}=$
11263.sol:
$x^5-5 x^4+9 x^3-9 x^2+5 x-1=0$ ...(i) $\because a_0 x^{\mathrm{n}}+a_1 x^{\mathrm{n}-1}+a_2 x^{\mathrm{n}-2}+\ldots .+a_{\mathrm{n}-1} x+a_{\mathrm{n}}=0$
Here $a_0=-a_{\mathrm{n}}, a_1=-a_{\mathrm{n}-1}$ is class II reciprocal equation. So, eq (i) is an odd degree reciprocal equation By inspection $x=1$ is a root Using synthetic division $\begin{array}{c|cccccc}$1 & 1 & -5 & 9 & -9 & 5 & -1 \\& 0 & 1 & -4 & 5 & -4 & 1 \\\hline & 1 & -4 & 5 & -4 & 1 & 0\end{array} $x^4-4 x^3+5 x^2-4 x+1=0$ ...(ii) Equation (ii) is an even degree reciprocal equation of class I. $\frac{x^4-4 x^3+5 x^2-4 x+1}{x^2}=0 \Rightarrow\left(x^2+\frac{1}{x^2}\right)-4\left(x+\frac{1}{x}\right)+5=0$....(iii) Let $x+\frac{1}{x}=a$. So, Eq (iii) implies. $\begin{array}{ll} \left(a^2-2\right)-4 a+5=0 \Rightarrow(a-3)(a-1)=0 \\ \Rightarrow a=1 \text{ or } a=3 & a=3 \\ \Rightarrow a=1 & x+\frac{1}{x}=3 \\ \Rightarrow x+\frac{1}{x}=1 & \Rightarrow x^2-3 x+1=0 \\ \Rightarrow x^2-x+1=0 & x=\frac{3 \pm \sqrt{5}}{2} \end{array} \\ So, $\alpha_1=1, \alpha_2=$\frac{1+i \sqrt{3}}{2}, \alpha_$3=$\frac{1-i \sqrt{3}}{2}\begin{aligned}$& \alpha_4=$\frac{3+\sqrt{5}}{2}, \alpha_$5=$\frac{3-\sqrt{5}}{2}$\\ & $\frac{1}{\alpha_1^2}+\frac{1}{\alpha_2^2}+\frac{1}{\alpha_3^2}+\frac{1}{\alpha_4^2}+\frac{1}{\alpha_5^2}=$1+$\left(\frac{2}{1+i \sqrt{3}}\right)^$2+ \\ & \qquad$\left(\frac{2}{1-i \sqrt{3}}\right)^$2+$\left(\frac{2}{3+\sqrt{5}}\right)^$2+$\left(\frac{2}{3-\sqrt{5}}\right)^$2 \\ & =1+$\frac{(2-2 i \sqrt{3})^2}{16}+\frac{(2+2 i \sqrt{3})^2}{16}+\frac{(6-2 \sqrt{5})^2}{16}+\frac{(6+2 \sqrt{5})^2}{16}$\\ & =1+$\frac{4-12+4-12+36+20+36+20}{16}=$1+6=7 \end{aligned}

11418.text: If the roots of the equation \(a x^2+a x+c=0\) are in the ratio \(p: q\), then \(\sqrt{\frac{p}{q}}+\sqrt{\frac{q}{p}}=\)
11418.sol:
Equation given be,
\(\begin{aligned}
a x^2+a x+c & =0 \\
\therefore \text{ Sum of roots }=-\frac{a}{a} & =-1
\end{aligned}\)
\(\therefore\) Sum of roots \(=-\frac{a}{a}=-1\)
and product of roots \(=\frac{c}{a}\).
Now roots are given in ratio \(\frac{p}{q}\),
i.e., \(\frac{\alpha}{\beta}=\frac{p}{q}\)
So,
\(\begin{aligned}
\sqrt{\frac{p}{q}}+\sqrt{\frac{q}{p}} & =\sqrt{\frac{\alpha}{\beta}}+\sqrt{\frac{\beta}{\alpha}} \\
& =\frac{\alpha+\beta}{\sqrt{\alpha \beta}}=\frac{-1}{ \pm \sqrt{\frac{c}{a}}}=-\sqrt{\frac{a}{c}} \text{ or } \sqrt{\frac{a}{c}}
\end{aligned}\)

initial speed \(u\) of emitted electron is calculated as
\(v²=u²-2 a s \Rightarrow 0=u²-2 a \times1 \Rightarrow u²=2 a=\frac{2 q E}{m}\)

20401.text: Which of the following reactions is an example for incomplete combustion?
20401.sol:
Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon involves the reaction of the fuel with sufficient oxygen to produce carbon dioxide and water as the only products. Incomplete combustion occurs when there is insufficient oxygen, leading to the formation of products like carbon monoxide or elemental carbon (soot) instead of carbon dioxide.

Analyzing the given reactions:
1. The first reaction is $\text{C}_{4}\text{H}_{10} + \dfrac{13}{2}\text{O}_{2} \rightarrow 4\text{CO}_{2} + 5\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$. This is complete combustion of butane.
2. The second reaction is the oxidation of isobutane to tert-butyl alcohol using alkaline $\text{KMnO}_{4}$, which is a controlled oxidation, not combustion.
3. The third reaction is the controlled catalytic oxidation of methane to formaldehyde ($\text{HCHO}$), not combustion.
4. The fourth reaction is $\text{CH}_{4} + \text{O}_{2} \rightarrow \text{C(s)} + 2\text{H}_{2}\text{O(l)}$. Here, carbon is produced in the form of soot (solid carbon) instead of carbon dioxide, which is a characteristic feature of incomplete combustion of methane.

Answer:

20745.subject: Chemistry
20745.text: $5.8 \mathrm{ g}$ of a gas maintained at $95^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ occupies the same volume as $0.368 \mathrm{ g}$ of hydrogen gas maintained at a temperature of $17^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ and pressure being the same atmospheric pressure for both the gases. What is the molecular mass of the unknown gas?
20745.sol:
Using the ideal gas equation $PV = nRT$, where $n = \dfrac{w}{M}$, we have $V = \dfrac{wRT}{PM}$.

Since the volume $V$ and pressure $P$ are the same for both gases, we can write the equality:

$\dfrac{w_1 R T_1}{M_1 P} = \dfrac{w_2 R T_2}{M_2 P}$

Canceling $R$ and $P$ from both sides, we get:

$\dfrac{w_1 T_1}{M_1} = \dfrac{w_2 T_2}{M_2}$

Given values for the unknown gas: $w_1 = 5.8 \text{ g}$, $T_1 = 95 + 273 = 368 \text{ K}$.

Given values for hydrogen gas ($H_2$): $w_2 = 0.368 \text{ g}$, $T_2 = 17 + 273 = 290 \text{ K}$, $M_2 = 2 \text{ g/mol}$.

Substituting these values into the equation:

$\dfrac{5.8 \times 368}{M_1} = \dfrac{0.368 \times 290}{2}$

Solving for $M_1$:

$M_1 = \dfrac{5.8 \times 368 \times 2}{0.368 \times 290}$

$M_1 = \dfrac{5.8 \times 736}{106.72}$

$M_1 = \dfrac{4268.8}{106.72} = 40 \text{ g/mol}$

Answer: 40 g/mol

21933.subject: Mathematics
21933.text: A five-digits number is formed by using the digits $1,2,3,4,5$ with no repetition. The probability that the numbers 1 and 5 are always together, is
21933.sol:
The total number of ways to form a five-digit number using the digits $1, 2, 3, 4, 5$ without repetition is $5! = 120$.

To find the number of ways where $1$ and $5$ are always together, treat the pair $(1, 5)$ as a single unit. This leaves us with $4$ units: $\{1, 5\}, 2, 3, 4$.

The number of ways to arrange these $4$ units is $4! = 24$.

Within the unit $\{1, 5\}$, the digits $1$ and $5$ can be arranged in $2! = 2$ ways (either $15$ or $51$).

Therefore, the total number of favorable arrangements is $4! \times 2! = 24 \times 2 = 48$.

The probability is the ratio of favorable arrangements to total arrangements:

$P = \dfrac{48}{120} = \dfrac{2}{5}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{2}{5}$

22166.text:
Let P be a point on the line $L_1: \dfrac{x-2}{2} = y + 1 = \dfrac{z-1}{2}$ such that its distance from the point $A(2 , -1 , 1)$ is 6 units.
Given that $x$-coordinate of P is greater than 2,
Find the coordinates of point Q on the line $L_2: x - 1 = \dfrac{y-2}{2} = \dfrac{z-2}{2}$ such that Q is the closest point to P.
22166.sol:
The line $L_1$ is given by $\dfrac{x-2}{2} = \dfrac{y+1}{1} = \dfrac{z-1}{2}$.

The direction ratios of $L_1$ are $(2, 1, 2)$, so its direction cosines are $\left(\dfrac{2}{3}, \dfrac{1}{3}, \dfrac{2}{3}\right)$.

The point $A$ is $(2, -1, 1)$, which lies on $L_1$. Since $P$ is at a distance of $6$ units from $A$, the coordinates of $P$ are given by:

$\left(2 \pm 6 \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right), -1 \pm6 \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right),1 $\pm6$\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)\right)

Since$ the x$-coordinate of $P$ is greater than 2$, we take the positive sign:

$P = (2 + 4, -1 + 2, 1 + 4) = (6, 1, 5)$

The line $L_2$ is given by $\dfrac{x-1}{1} = \dfrac{y-2}{2} = \dfrac{z-2}{2}$.

Let $ Q$ be a point on $L_2$. Its coordinates can be written as $Q(t+1, 2t+2, 2t+2)$ for some parameter $t$.

For $Q$ to be the closest point to $P, the $vector \overrightarrow{PQ} must be perpendicular$ to the direction vector of L_2$, which is $\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$.

\overrightarrow{PQ} = ($t+1-6)\hat{i} + (2t+2-1)\hat{j} + (2t+2-5)\hat{k} = (t-5)\hat{i} + (2t+1)\hat{j} + (2t-3)\hat{k}

Taking the $dot product of \overrightarrow{PQ} and the direction vector of$ L_2$ to be zero:

$1(t-5) + 2(2t+1) + 2(2t-3) = 0$

$t - 5 + 4t + 2 + 4t - 6 = 0$

$9t - 9 = 0 \Rightarrow t = 1$

Substituting $t = 1$ into the coordinates of $Q$, we get:

$Q = (1+1, 2(1)+2, 2(1)+2) = (2, 4, 4)$

Answer: $(2 , 4 , 4)$

22323.text: The vector that must be added to $\hat{\mathrm{i}}-3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{k}}$ and $3 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+6 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-7 \hat{\mathrm{k}}$ so resultant vector is a unit vector along the $X$ - axis is
22323.sol:
Let the given vectors be $\vec{A} = \hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{B} = 3\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} - 7\hat{k}$.

Let the vector to be added be $\vec{V} = x\hat{i} + y\hat{j} + z\hat{k}$.

The resultant vector is a unit vector along the X-axis, which is $\hat{i}$.

Therefore, $\vec{A} + \vec{B} + \vec{V} = \hat{i}$.

$(\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}) + (3\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} - 7\hat{k}) + (x\hat{i} + y\hat{j} + z\hat{k}) = \hat{i}$.

$(1 + 3 + x)\hat{i} + (-3 + 6 + y)\hat{j} + (2 - 7 + z)\hat{k} = \hat{i}$.

$(4 + x)\hat{i} + (3 + y)\hat{j} + (-5 + z)\hat{k} = 1\hat{i} + 0\hat{j} + 0\hat{k}$.

Equating the components:

$4 + x = 1 \Rightarrow x = -3$

$3 + y = 0 \Rightarrow y = -3$

$-5 + z = 0 \Rightarrow z = 5$

25886.subject: Mathematics
25886.text:
Let $L$ be the straight line joining the points $P(1, 2, -1)$ and $Q(2, 3, 1)$. Let $S$ be the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the point $R(4, -1, 5)$ to the line $L$. Another line passing through $R$ intersects $L$ at a point $T$ such that the point $S$ divides the line segment $PT$ internally in the ratio $|PS| : |ST| = 1 : 2$, where $|PS|$ and $|ST|$ are the lengths of the line segments $PS$ and $ST$, respectively.
Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE ?
options: The orthocentre of the triangle $PRT$ is $\left(\dfrac{23}{5}, -4, \dfrac{31}{5}\right)$
The orthocentre of the triangle $PRT$ is $(4, 3, 5)$
The area of the triangle $PRT$ is $6\sqrt{5}$
The area of the triangle $PRT$ is $18\sqrt{5}$
25886.sol:
The direction ratios of line $L$ passing through $P(1, 2, -1)$ and $Q(2, 3, 1)$ are $(2-1, 3-2, 1-(-1)) = (1, 1, 2)$.

The equation of line $L$ is $\dfrac{x-1}{1} = \dfrac{y-2}{1} = \dfrac{z+1}{2} = \lambda$.

Any point on $L$ can be written as $S(\lambda+1, \lambda+2, 2\lambda-1)$.

Since $S$ is the foot of the perpendicular from $R(4, -1, 5)$ to $L$, the direction ratios of $RS$ are $(\lambda-3, \lambda+3, 2\lambda-6)$.

As $RS \perp L$, the dot product of their direction ratios is zero:

$1(\lambda-3) + 1(\lambda+3) + 2(2\lambda-6) = 0$

$6\lambda - 12 = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = 2$

Thus, the coordinates of $S$ are $(3, 4, 3)$.

The length of $PS$ is $\sqrt{(3-1)^2 + (4-2)^2 + (3-(-1))^2} = \sqrt{4+4+16} = 2\sqrt{6}$.

The length of the altitude $RS$ is $\sqrt{(3-4)^2 + (4-(-1))^2 + (3-5)^2} = \sqrt{1+25+4} = \sqrt{30}$.

Since $S$ divides $PT$ internally in the ratio $1:2$, we have:

$S = \dfrac{T + 2P}{3} \Rightarrow T = 3S - 2P$

$T = 3(3, 4, 3) - 2(1, 2, -1) = (7, 8, 11)$

The length of the base $PT$ is $3|PS| = 6\sqrt{6}$.

The area of $\triangle PRT$ is $\dfrac{1}{2} \times |PT| \times |RS| = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 6\sqrt{6} \times \sqrt{30} = 18\sqrt{5}$.

The orthocentre $H$ lies on the altitude $RS$. The line $RS$ passes through $S(3, 4, 3)$ and has direction ratios proportional to $R-S = (1, -5, 2)$.

Let the coordinates of $H$ be $(3+t, 4-5t, 3+2t)$.

Since $H$ is the orthocentre, $PH \perp RT$.

The direction ratios of $RT$ are $(7-4, 8-(-1), 11-5) = (3, 9, 6)$, which is proportional to $(1, 3, 2)$.

The direction ratios of $PH$ are $(3+t-1, 4-5t-2, 3+2t-(-1)) = (t+2, 2-5t, 2t+4)$.

Taking the dot product of $PH$ and $RT$:

$1(t+2) + 3(2-5t) + 2(2t+4) = 0$

$t + 2 + 6 - 15t + 4t + 8 = 0$

$16 - 10t = 0 \Rightarrow t = \dfrac{8}{5}$

Substituting $t = \dfrac{8}{5}$ into the coordinates of $H$, we get:

$H = \left(3 + \dfrac{8}{5}, 4 - 5\left(\dfrac{8}{5}\right), 3 + 2\left(\dfrac{8}{5}\right)\right) = \left(\dfrac{23}{5}, -4, \dfrac{31}{5}\right)$

Answer: The orthocentre of the triangle $PRT$ is $\left(\dfrac{23}{5}, -4, \dfrac{31}{5}\right)$; The area of the triangle $PRT$ is $18\sqrt{5}$

26096.subject: Physics
26096.text:
The figure shows a circuit having eight resistances of $1Ω$ each, labelled ${R}_{1}$ to ${R}_{8}$, and two ideal batteries with voltages ${ε}_{1} = 12V$ and ${ε}_{2} = 6V$.

Which of the following statement(s) is(are) correct?
options: The magnitude of current flowing through ${R}_{1}$ is $7 . 2A$.
The magnitude of current flowing through ${R}_{2}$ is $1 . 2A$.
The magnitude of current flowing through ${R}_{3}$ is $4 . 8A$.
The magnitude of current flowing through ${R}_{5}$ is $2 . 4A$.
26096.sol:
Point $A$ and $B$ are at same potential so they can be merged/folded.

Now, let& $x$ and& $y$ be the current flowing from& $6V$ and& $12V$ batteries.

The current distribution is shown below.

Applying Kirchhoff's voltage law,

For loop& $1:$

$- \dfrac{1}{2}x - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(x + y\right) - 1x + 6 = 0$

$⇒ - 2x - \dfrac{y}{2} = - 6$

$⇒ - 4x - y = - 12$

$⇒ 4x + y = 12 ⋯ \left(1\right)$

For loop $2:$

$\dfrac{1}{2}$ y + 1y + 12 + $\dfrac{1}{2}\left($ x + y\right) = 0$

\dfrac{3}{2}$ y + $\dfrac{y}{2} + \dfrac{x}{2} = -12$

$2y + \dfrac{x}{2} = -12$

$4y + x = - 24 ⋯ \left(2\right)$

Using, $\left(2\right) - 4 \times\left(1\right)$, we have

$4y + x - 16x - 4y= - 24 - 48$

$⇒ - 15x = - 72$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{72}{15}$

Putting in equation $\left(1\right)$,

$4\left(\dfrac{72}{15}\right) +y = 12$

$⇒ y = 12 - \dfrac{288}{15}= \dfrac{180 - 288}{15}= \dfrac{- 108}{15} = -7 . 2A$

Now, current in ${R}_{1} = 7 . 2A$

Current in ${R}_{2} = \dfrac{x + y}{2} = \left(\dfrac{72}{15} - \dfrac{108}{15}\right)\dfrac{1}{2}= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{36}{15}\right) = \dfrac{2 . 4}{2}A$

$= 1 . 2A$

Current in ${R}_{3} = x = 4 . 8A$

Current in ${R}_{5} = \dfrac{1}{2}x = 2 . 4A$

26597.text:
A thin rod of mass $M$ and length $a$ is free to rotate in horizontal plane about a fixed vertical axis passing through point $O$. A thin circular disc of mass $M$ and of radius $\dfrac{a}{4}$ is pivoted on this rod with its centre at a distance $\dfrac{a}{4}$ from the free end so that it can rotate freely about its vertical axis, as shown in the figure. Assume that both the rod and the disc have uniform density and they remain horizontal during the motion. An outside stationary conserver finds the rod rotating with an angular velocity $Ω$ and the disc rotating about its vertical axis with angular velocity $4Ω$. The total angular momentum of the system about the point $O$ is $\left[\left(\dfrac{M{a}^{2}Ω}{48}\right)$n\right]$.

The value of $n$ is _________ .$
26597.sol:
Angular momentum of the system about $O$,

$\overset{\to}{L} = \overset{\to}{L}Rod + \overset{\to}{L}Disc$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{L} = \overset{\to}{L}Rod + \left[{\left(\overset{\to}{L}CM\right)}_{Disc} + \overset{\to}{r}CM \times \left({M}_{Disc}\overset{\to}{V}CM\right)\right]$

$⇒ L = \dfrac{M{a}^{2}Ω}{3} + \dfrac{M{a}^{2}}{8}Ω + M\left(\dfrac{3a}{4}\right)Ω\left(\dfrac{3a}{4}\right)$

$⇒ L = \dfrac{M{a}^{2}}{3}Ω + \dfrac{M{a}^{2}}{8}Ω + \dfrac{9M{a}^{2}}{16}Ω$

$⇒ L = \dfrac{16M{a}^{2}Ω + 6M{a}^{2}Ω + 27M{a}^{2}Ω}{48}$

$⇒ L = \dfrac{49}{48}M{a}^{2}Ω$

Compare it with $\dfrac{nM{a}^{2}}{48}Ω$, we get $n = 49$

Hence, $n = 49$

33274.sol:
The given equation is:

$(1 - x^3)^{10} = \sum\limits_{r=0}^{10} a_r x^r (1-x)^{30-2r}$

Using the algebraic identity $1 - x^3 = (1-x)(1+x+x^2)$, the left hand side can be written as:

$(1-x)^{10}(1+x+x^2)^{10} = \sum\limits_{r=0}^{10} a_r x^r (1-x)^{30-2r}$

Dividing both sides by $(1-x)^{30}$:

$\dfrac{(1-x)^{10}(1+x+x^2)^{10}}{(1-x)^{30}} = \sum\limits_{r=0}^{10} a_r \dfrac{x^r}{(1-x)^{2r}}$

$\left( \dfrac{1+x+x^2}{(1-x)^2} \right)^{10} = \sum\limits_{r=0}^{10} a_r \left( \dfrac{x}{(1-x)^2} \right)^r$

Let $y = \dfrac{x}{(1-x)^2}$.

The term inside the bracket on the left hand side can be simplified as:

$\dfrac{1+x+x^2}{(1-x)^2} = \dfrac{1-2x+x^2+3x}{(1-x)^2} = \dfrac{(1-x)^2+3x}{(1-x)^2} = 1 + 3\left(\dfrac{x}{(1-x)^2}\right) = 1 + 3y$

Substituting this into the equation, we get:

$(1 + 3y)^{10} = \sum\limits_{r=0}^{10} a_r y^r$

Using the binomial expansion, $(1 + 3y)^{10} = \sum\limits_{r=0}^{10} {^{10}C_{r}} (3y)^r = \sum\limits_{r=0}^{10} {^{10}C_{r}} 3^r y^r$.

Comparing the coefficients of $y^r$ on both sides, we obtain:

$a_r = {^{10}C_{r}} 3^r$

For $r = 9$ and $r = 10$:

$a_9 = {^{10}C_{9}} 3^9 = 10 \times 3^9$

$a_{10} = {^{10}C_{10}} 3^{10} = 1 \times 3^{10} = 3^{10}$

Therefore, the required value is:

$\dfrac{9a_9}{a_{10}} = \dfrac{9 \times 10 \times 3^9}{3^{10}} = \dfrac{90 \times 3^9}{3 \times 3^9} = \dfrac{90}{3} = 30$

Answer: $30$

34650.text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $\sec x \frac{\mathrm{~d} y}{\mathrm{~d} x}-2 y=2+3 \sin x, x \in\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$, $y(0)=-\frac{7}{4}$. Then $y\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)$ is equal to :
34650.sol:
The differential equation is $\sec x \frac{dy}{dx} - 2y = 2 + 3\sin x$, or $\frac{dy}{dx} - 2\cos x \cdot y = (2 + 3\sin x)\cos x$.
This is a linear ODE with integrating factor $\mu(x) = e^{-2\sin x}$.
Multiplying both sides and integrating: $\frac{d}{dx}[ye^{-2\sin x}] = (2 + 3\sin x)\cos x \cdot e^{-2\sin x}$
Computing the integral: $\int 2\cos x \cdot e^{-2\sin x} dx = -e^{-2\sin x}$
For the second term, using integration by parts: $\int 3\sin x \cos x \cdot e^{-2\sin x} dx = \frac{3}{4}e^{-2\sin x}(-2\sin x - 1)$
Thus: $ye^{-2\sin x} = -e^{-2\sin x} + \frac{3}{4}e^{-2\sin x}(-2\sin x - 1) + C$
Simplifying: $y = -\frac{7}{4} - \frac{3}{2}\sin x + Ce^{2\sin x}$
Using $y(0) = -\frac{7}{4}$ gives $C = 0$.
Therefore: $y(\frac{\pi}{6}) = -\frac{7}{4} - \frac{3}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{2} = -\frac{5}{2}$

34723.text: Let $y = y ( x )$ be the solution of the differential equation $\left(3{y}^{2} - 5{x}^{2}\right)ydx + 2x\left({x}^{2} - {y}^{2}\right)dy = 0$ such that $y ( 1 ) = 1$. Then $\left|( y ( 2 ) {)}^{3} - 12y ( 2 )\right|$ is equal to :
34723.sol:

$\left(3{y}^{2} - 5{x}^{2}\right)ydx + 2x\left({x}^{2} - {y}^{2}\right)dy = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y\left(5{x}^{2} - 3{y}^{2}\right)}{2x\left({x}^{2} - {y}^{2}\right)}$

This is homogeneous differential equation

Let $y = tx ⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = t + x\dfrac{dt}{dx}$

$t + x\dfrac{dt}{dx} = \dfrac{( tx ) \left(5{x}^{2} - 3{t}^{2}{x}^{2}\right)}{2x\left({x}^{2} - {t}^{2}{x}^{2}\right)} = \dfrac{t\left(5 - 3{t}^{2}\right)}{2\left(1 - {t}^{2}\right)}$

$⇒ x\dfrac{dt}{dx} = \dfrac{5t - 3{t}^{3}}{2 - 2{t}^{2}} - t = \dfrac{3t - {t}^{3}}{2 - 2{t}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{2\left(1 - {t}^{2}\right)}{3t - {t}^{3}}dt = \dfrac{1}{x}dx$

$∫ \dfrac{2\left(1 - {t}^{2}\right)}{3t - {t}^{3}}dt = ∫ \dfrac{1}{x}dx . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Now let $3t - {t}^{3} = z ⇒ 3\left(1 - {t}^{2}\right)dt = dz$

$⇒ \left(1 - {t}^{2}\right)dt = \dfrac{1}{3}dz$

Substitute in equation $\left(1\right)$ we get,

$\dfrac{2}{3} ∫ \dfrac{dz}{z} = ∫ \dfrac{1}{x}dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{2}{3}ln ( z ) = lnx + lnc$

$⇒ z\dfrac{2}{3} = cx ⇒ z = c\dfrac{3}{2}x\dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ 3t - {t}^{3} = c\dfrac{3}{2}x\dfrac{3}{2}$

Now put $t = \dfrac{y}{x}$

$⇒ \dfrac{3y}{x} - \dfrac{{y}^{3}}{{x}^{3}} = c\dfrac{3}{2}x\dfrac{3}{2}$

Given $y ( 1 ) = 1$ when $x = 1, y = 1$

$⇒ c\dfrac{3}{2} = 2$

So, equation becomes $3\dfrac{y}{x} - \dfrac{{y}^{3}}{{x}^{3}} = 2x\dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ 3{x}^{2}y - {y}^{3} = 2x\dfrac{9}{2} . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

Put $x = 2$ in equation $\left(2\right)$,

$12y ( 2 ) - {\left(y ( 2 )\right)}^{3} = 2 ( 2) \dfrac{9}{2} = 32\sqrt{2}$

$∴ \left|{\left(y ( 2 )\right)}^{3} - 12y ( 2 )\right| = 32\sqrt{2}$

$= \dfrac{3K{q}^{2}}{4{r}^{2}} = \dfrac{3F}{4}$

42106.subject: Physics
42106.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R)
Assertion (A) : The property of body, by virtue of which it tends to regain its original shape when the external force is removed, is Elasticity.
Reason (R) : The restoring force depends upon the bonded inter atomic and inter molecular force of solid.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
42106.sol:
Elasticity is the ability of a material to deform under stress and then return to its original shape when the stress is removed.

The restoring force in elastic materials is associated with the inter-atomic or inter-molecular forces that act to bring the atoms or molecules back to their original positions when the material is deformed. When an external force is applied to a material, it causes a displacement of atoms or molecules from their equilibrium positions. The restoring force is a result of the potential energy stored in these inter-atomic or inter-molecular bonds, and it works to bring the material back to its original state.

Hence, both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation (A)

44381.subject: Physics
44381.text: The velocity of sound in air is doubled when the temperature is raised from $0^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $\alpha^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The value of $\alpha$ is $\_\_\_\_$.
44381.sol:
The velocity of sound in air depends on temperature as $v \propto \sqrt{T}$ (absolute temperature).
If the velocity doubles:
$\frac{v_2}{v_1} = 2 = \sqrt{\frac{T_2}{T_1}}$.
Squaring: $\frac{T_2}{T_1} = 4$.
With $T_1 = 0°C = 273.15$ K and $T_2 = 273.15 + \alpha$ K:
$\frac{273.15 + \alpha}{273.15} = 4$, giving $273.15 + \alpha = 1092.6$ K.
Therefore $\alpha = 819.45°C \approx 819°C$.

According to VSEPR theory, the electron pairs in the valence shell of the central atom repel each other to minimize electron-electron repulsion.

Lone pairs (Lp) are localized on the central atom and are attracted by only one nucleus, so they occupy more space and exert greater repulsion.

Bond pairs (Bp) are shared between two atoms and are attracted by two nuclei, so they occupy less space and exert lesser repulsion.

Thus, the correct order of repulsion between electron pairs is $\text{Lp-Lp} > \text{Lp-Bp} > \text{Bp-Bp}$.

Answer: $\text{Lp-Lp} > \text{Lp-Bp} > \text{Bp-Bp}$

56028.subject: Chemistry
56028.text: If Instantaneous rate of reaction is stated as $-\frac{1}{2} \frac{\mathrm{ d}[x]}{\mathrm{dt}}=-\frac{\mathrm{d}[\mathrm{y}]}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{1}{2} \frac{\mathrm{ d}[\mathrm{z}]}{\mathrm{dt}}$, identify the reaction.
56028.sol:
The instantaneous rate expression provides direct insight into the reaction stoichiometry. For a general reaction $aA + bB \rightarrow cC + dD$, the rate is defined as $\text{Rate} = -\frac{1}{a} \frac{d[A]}{dt} = -\frac{1}{b} \frac{d[B]}{dt} = +\frac{1}{c} \frac{d[C]}{dt} = +\frac{1}{d} \frac{d[D]}{dt}$.

Given the rate expression $-\frac{1}{2} \frac{d[x]}{dt} = -\frac{d[y]}{dt} = \frac{1}{2} \frac{d[z]}{dt}$, the stoichiometric coefficients are determined by the denominators. The negative terms indicate reactants, while the positive term indicates a product.

The balanced reaction must be $2x + y \rightarrow 2z$, which corresponds to option B.

56039.subject: Chemistry
56039.text: Which of the following is an example of first order reaction?
56039.sol:
Reaction order is an experimentally determined quantity describing how rate depends on reactant concentrations. A first-order reaction exhibits a rate linearly dependent on a single reactant concentration, or one where the sum of concentration exponents in the rate law equals one.

Considering each option:

A) $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CHO}_{(\mathrm{g})} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_{4(\mathrm{ g})}+\mathrm{CO}_{(\mathrm{g})}$: Acetaldehyde decomposition may follow first-order kinetics at high temperatures but exhibits complex behavior and is not universally first-order.

B) $2\mathrm{NO}_{2(\mathrm{ g})}+\mathrm{F}_{2(\mathrm{ g})} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NO}_2\mathrm{ F}_{(\mathrm{g})}$: The rate law is Rate $= k[\mathrm{NO}_2][\mathrm{F}_2]$, with exponent sum $1+1=2$, indicating second-order kinetics.

C) $2\mathrm{NO}_{(\mathrm{g})}+2\mathrm{H}_{2(\mathrm{ g})} \rightarrow \mathrm{N}_{2(\mathrm{ g})}+2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_{(\mathrm{g})}$: The rate law is Rate $= k[\mathrm{NO}]^2[\mathrm{H}_2]$, with exponent sum $2+1=3$, making it third-order.

D) $2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_{2(\ell)} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_{(\ell)}+\mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{ g})}$: Hydrogen peroxide decomposition has the rate law Rate $= k[\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2]$, with exponent 1, confirming it as a first-order reaction.

Option D is the unambiguous example of first-order kinetics.

57610.subject: Chemistry
57610.text: Which of the following has highest reactivity for SN reactions?
57610.sol:
Reactivity in SN reactions depends on the mechanism pathway: SN1 favors tertiary alkyl halides due to carbocation stability, while SN2 favors primary alkyl halides due to minimal steric hindrance.

n-Butyl iodide (primary) and isobutyl iodide (primary with beta-branching) undergo SN2 readily but are unreactive in SN1 due to unstable primary carbocations. sec-Butyl iodide (secondary) reacts through both mechanisms but with moderate rates.

Tertiary alkyl halides like tert-butyl iodide undergo rapid SN1 reactions, as the tertiary carbocation intermediate is highly stabilized. Steric hindrance prevents SN2 reactivity, but the SN1 pathway dominates under favorable conditions, making tertiary halides the most reactive overall.

The ranking is: tert-butyl iodide > sec-butyl iodide > n-butyl iodide > isobutyl iodide.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{D}}$

59141.subject: Chemistry
59141.text: Calculate the number of moles of nonvolatile solute dissolved in 0.5 kg solvent if molal elevation constant for solvent is $2 \mathrm{ kg} \mathrm{ K} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}  \left[\Delta \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{b}}=0.8 \mathrm{ K}\right]$
59141.sol:
The number of moles is determined using the boiling point elevation formula $\Delta T_b = K_b m$, with $\Delta T_b = 0.8\text{ K}$ and $K_b = 2\text{ kg K mol}^{-1}$.

Molality $m$ relates to moles $n$ and solvent mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ as $m = n / 0.5$.

Substituting into the elevation formula:
$0.8 = 2 \cdot \frac{n}{0.5}$

Solving for $n$:
$n = \frac{0.8 \times 0.5}{2} = \frac{0.4}{2} = 0.2\text{ mol}$

The number of moles of nonvolatile solute is $\boxed{0.2}$.

62542.sol:
We have $y = \tan^{-1}\sqrt{\dfrac{1 + \sin 2x}{1 - \sin 2x}}$.

Using the trigonometric identities $1 + \sin 2x = (\cos x + \sin x)^2$ and $1 - \sin 2x = (\cos x - \sin x)^2$, we get:

$y = \tan^{-1}\sqrt{\dfrac{(\cos x + \sin x)^2}{(\cos x - \sin x)^2}} = \tan^{-1}\left| \dfrac{\cos x + \sin x}{\cos x - \sin x} \right|$

At $x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$, $\cos \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ and $\sin \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}$. Since $\cos x > \sin x$, the expression inside the modulus is positive.

$y = \tan^{-1}\left( \dfrac{\cos x + \sin x}{\cos x - \sin x} \right)$

Dividing the numerator and the denominator by $\cos x$:

$y = \tan^{-1}\left( \dfrac{1 + \tan x}{1 - \tan x} \right)$

$y = \tan^{-1}\left( \tan\left( \dfrac{\pi}{4} + x \right) \right)$

For $x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$, $\dfrac{\pi}{4} + x = \dfrac{5\pi}{12}$, which lies in the principal branch $\left( -\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2} \right)$.

$y = \dfrac{\pi}{4} + x$

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} = 1$

Answer: $1$

65150.text: Let $\bar{a}, \overline{\mathrm{ b}}$ and $\overline{\mathrm{c}}$ be vectors of magnitude 2,3 and 4 respectively. If $\bar{a}$ is perpendicular to $(\overline{\mathrm{b}}+\overline{\mathrm{c}}), \overline{\mathrm{b}}$ is perpendicular to $(\overline{\mathrm{c}}+\bar{a})$ and $\overline{\mathrm{c}}$ is perpendicular to (\bar{a}+\bar{b}$ ), then the magnitude of \bar{a}+\overline{\mathrm{b}}+\overline{\mathrm{c}}$ is
65150.sol:
Given vector magnitudes: $|\bar{a}| = 2$, $|\bar{b}| = 3$, $|\bar{c}| = 4$.
The perpendicularity conditions yield the dot product equations:
$\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} + \bar{a} \cdot \bar{c} = 0$
$\bar{b} \cdot \bar{c} + \bar{b} \cdot \bar{a} = 0$
$\bar{c} \cdot \bar{a} + \bar{c} \cdot \bar{b} = 0$

Let $x = \bar{a} \cdot \bar{b}$, $y = \bar{b} \cdot \bar{c}$, $z = \bar{c} \cdot \bar{a}$. The system becomes:
$x + z = 0$
$y + x = 0$
$z + y = 0$

From the first equation, $z = -x$. From the second, $y = -x$. Substituting into the third gives $z + y = -x + (-x) = -2x = 0$, so $x = 0$.
Hence $y = 0$ and $z = 0$, confirming the vectors are mutually orthogonal.

The magnitude of the sum is found from:
$|\bar{a} + \bar{b} + \bar{c}|^2 = |\bar{a}|^2 + |\bar{b}|^2 + |\bar{c}|^2 + 2(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} + \bar{b} \cdot \bar{c} + \bar{c} \cdot \bar{a}) = 4 + 9 + 16 + 0 = 29$

Thus $|\bar{a} + \bar{b} + \bar{c}| = \sqrt{29}$, corresponding to option C.

66315.subject: Physics
66315.text: If a galvanometer is shunted by $\left(\dfrac{1}{n-1}\right)^{th}$ of the value of its resistance, then the fraction of the total current passing through the galvanometer is
66315.sol:
Let the resistance of the galvanometer be $G$ and the total current in the circuit be $I$.

The shunt resistance is given as $S = \dfrac{G}{n-1}$.

Since the galvanometer and the shunt are connected in parallel, the potential difference across them is equal:

$I_g G = (I - I_g) S$

Substituting the value of $S$:

$I_g G = (I - I_g) \dfrac{G}{n-1}$

$I_g (n-1) = I - I_g$

$n I_g - I_g + I_g = I$

$n I_g = I$

$\dfrac{I_g}{I} = \dfrac{1}{n}$

The fraction of the total current passing through the galvanometer is $\dfrac{1}{n}.$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{n}$

66588.subject: Physics
66588.text: Light of wavelength $\lambda$ strikes a photoelectric surface and electrons are ejected with energy E. If E is to be increased to twice the original value, the wavelength changes to $\lambda_1$
66588.sol:
The kinetic energy $E$ of ejected electrons is given by $E = hf - \phi$, with frequency $f = c/\lambda$, so:

$E = \frac{hc}{\lambda} - \phi$

When the energy doubles to $2E$ with wavelength $\lambda_1$:

$2E = \frac{hc}{\lambda_1} - \phi$

Substituting $\frac{hc}{\lambda} = E + \phi$ yields:

$\frac{hc}{\lambda_1} = 2\left(\frac{hc}{\lambda} - \phi\right) + \phi = \frac{2hc}{\lambda} - \phi$

Since $\phi > 0$, this implies $\frac{hc}{\lambda_1} < \frac{2hc}{\lambda}$. Dividing both sides by $hc$ preserves the inequality:

$\frac{1}{\lambda_1} < \frac{2}{\lambda}$

Taking reciprocals (and reversing the inequality since wavelengths are positive):

$\lambda_1 > \frac{\lambda}{2}$

This corresponds to option C.

67536.text: A block of mass M is lying on a horizontal frictionless surface. One end of the uniform rope of half the mass of the block is fixed to the block which is pulled in the horizontal direction by applying a force F at the other end. The tension in the middle of the rope will be
67536.sol:
Mass of the block = $M$

Mass of the rope = $\dfrac{M}{2}$

Total mass of the system = $M + \dfrac{M}{2} = \dfrac{3M}{2}$

Acceleration of the system $a = \dfrac{F}{\dfrac{3M}{2}} = \dfrac{2F}{3M}$

The tension in the middle of the rope accelerates the block and the rear half of the rope.

Mass behind the middle point $m' = M + \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{M}{2}\right) = M + \dfrac{M}{4} = \dfrac{5M}{4}$

Tension at the middle of the rope $T = m' a = \left(\dfrac{5M}{4}\right)\left(\dfrac{2F}{3M}\right) = \dfrac{5F}{6}$

Answer: $\dfrac{5F}{6}$

68160.text: The excess pressure inside a soap bubble is 1.5 times the excess pressure inside a second soap bubble. The volume of the second bubble is ' $x$ ' times the volume of the first bubble. The value of ' $x$ ' is
68160.sol:
The excess pressure difference between soap bubbles follows $P = \frac{4T}{R}$, where $T$ is surface tension and $R$ the radius.
Given $P_1 = \frac{3}{2}P_2$, substituting the pressure formula yields:

$\frac{4T}{R_1} = \frac{3}{2} \cdot \frac{4T}{R_2}$

Canceling $4T$ and rearranging gives $\frac{R_2}{R_1} = \frac{3}{2}$.

Since volume scales as $R^3$, the volume ratio is:

$x = \left(\frac{R_2}{R_1}\right)^3 = \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{27}{8}$.

The correct choice is D.

68511.subject: Physics
68511.text: A particle of mass $m$ is moving in a circular path of constant radius $r$ such that its centripetal acceleration $a_c$ is varying with time $t$ as, $a_c = k^2 r t^2$. The power delivered to the particle by the forces acting on it is (K$ = constant)$
68511.sol:
Given centripetal acceleration $a_c = k^2 r t^2$

Using the formula $a_c = \dfrac{v^2}{r}$:

$\dfrac{v^2}{r} = k^2 r t^2$

$v^2 = k^2 r^2 t^2$

$v = k r t$

The kinetic energy of the particle is given by:

$E = \dfrac{1}{2} m v^2$

$E = \dfrac{1}{2} m (k r t)^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} m k^2 r^2 t^2$

The total power delivered by all forces acting on the particle is equal to the rate of change of its kinetic energy:

$P = \dfrac{dE}{dt}$

$P = \dfrac{d}{dt} \left( \dfrac{1}{2}$ m k² r² t² \right)$

$P = $\dfrac{1}{2}$ m k² r² (2t)$

$P = m k² r² t$$

68652.subject: Physics
68652.text: A simple pendulum of length $l_1$ has periodic time $2.4$ s. Another simple pendulum of length $l_2 < l_1$, has periodic time $1.8$ s. The periodic time of simple pendulum of length $(l_1 - l_2)$ is nearly
68652.sol:
The time period of a simple pendulum is given by $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}}$.

Squaring both sides, we get $T^2 = \dfrac{4\pi^2 l}{g}$, which implies $l = \dfrac{g T^2}{4\pi^2}$.

For the first pendulum, $l_1 = \dfrac{g T_1^2}{4\pi^2}$.

For the second pendulum, $l_2 = \dfrac{g T_2^2}{4\pi^2}$.

For the pendulum of length $l_1 - l_2$, the time period $T$ is given by:

$T^2 = \dfrac{4\pi^2}{g} (l_1 - l_2) = \dfrac{4\pi^2}{g} \left( \dfrac{g T_1^2}{4\pi^2} - \dfrac{g T_2^2}{4\pi^2} \right) = T_1^2 - T_2^2$

Substituting the given values $T_1 = 2.4$ s and $T_2 = 1.8$ s:

$T^2 = (2.4)^2 - (1.8)^2 = 5.76 - 3.24 = 2.52$

$T = \sqrt{2.52} \approx 1.587$ s

This is nearly $1.6$ s.

Answer: $1.6$ s

69189.subject: Physics
69189.text: A bob of mass ' m ' is tied by a massless string whose other end is wound on a flywheel (disc) of radius ' $R$ ' and mass ' $m$ '. When released from the rest, the bob starts falling vertically downwards. If the bob has covered a vertical distance ' $h$ ', then angular speed of wheel will be (There is no slipping between string and wheel, $g$ - acceleration due to gravity)
69189.sol:
Conservation of mechanical energy is applied to the system, taking the initial state when the bob is at rest and the final state after it has fallen distance $h$.

Initial potential energy is $mgh$, with zero kinetic energy for both bob and flywheel. Final energy consists of translational kinetic energy $\frac{1}{2}mv^2$ for the bob and rotational kinetic energy $\frac{1}{2}I\omega^2$ for the flywheel.

For a solid disc, $I = \frac{1}{2}mR^2$. The no-slip condition gives $v = R\omega$.

Equating initial and final energies:

$mgh = \frac{1}{2}m(R\omega)^2 + \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{2}mR^2\right)\omega^2$

Simplifying yields:

$mgh = \frac{3}{4}mR^2\omega^2$

Solving for $\omega$:

$\omega^2 = \frac{4gh}{3R^2}$

$\omega = \frac{2}{R}\sqrt{\frac{gh}{3}}$

This corresponds to option A.

70165.subject: Physics
70165.text: Two light waves amplitudes in the ratio $3:1$ produce interference. The ratio of the maximum to minimum intensity is
70165.sol:
Let the amplitudes of the two light waves be $A_1$ and $A_2$.

Given $\dfrac{A_1}{A_2} = \dfrac{3}{1}$

The maximum intensity $I_\max$ is proportional to $(A_1 + A_2)^2$ and the minimum intensity $I_\min$ is proportional to $(A_1 - A_2)^2$.

$\dfrac{I_\max}{I_\min} = \dfrac{(A_1 + A_2)^2}{(A_1 - A_2)^2}$

Substituting the ratio of amplitudes:

$\dfrac{I_\max}{I_\min} = \dfrac{(3 + 1)^2}{(3 - 1)^2} = \dfrac{16}{4} = \dfrac{4}{1}$

The ratio of maximum to minimum intensity is $4 : 1$.

Answer: $4 : 1$

70443.subject: Physics
70443.text: The fundamental frequency of sonometer wire is $50$ Hz for some length and tension. If the length is increased by $25\%$ by keeping the tension same, then the frequency change of second harmonic is
70443.sol:
The fundamental frequency of a sonometer wire is given by $f = \dfrac{1}{2L} \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}}$.

Since tension $T$ and mass per unit length $\mu$ are constant, the frequency is inversely proportional to the length, $f \propto \dfrac{1}{L}$.

The frequency of the second harmonic is $f_2 = 2f$, which also follows $f_2 \propto \dfrac{1}{L}$.

When the length is increased by $25\%$, the new length becomes $L' = L + 0.25L = 1.25L = \dfrac{5}{4}L$.

The new frequency of the second harmonic is $f_2' = f_2 \times \dfrac{L}{L'} = f_2 \times \dfrac{4}{5} = 0.8 f_2$.

The percentage change in the frequency of the second harmonic is $\dfrac{f_2' - f_2}{f_2} \times 100\% = \dfrac{0.8 f_2 - f_2}{f_2} \times 100\% = -20\%$.

Thus, the frequency of the second harmonic decreases by $20\%$.

Answer: decrease by $20\%$

71102.subject: Biology
71102.text: Which one of the following is INCORRECT about genetic drift?
options: Genetic drift is also called the Sewall Wright Effect.
The effect of genetic drift is more significant in large populations.
Sometimes a few individuals become isolated from large populations and produce a small new population in a new geographical area.
71102.sol:
Genetic drift refers to the random fluctuations in allele frequencies from one generation to the next. It is a directionless process.

It is also known as the Sewall Wright effect.

The effect of genetic drift is highly significant in small populations, not large populations, because random changes have a much larger proportional impact when the number of individuals is small.

The founder effect is a type of genetic drift where a few individuals become isolated from a larger population and establish a new population in a different geographical area.

Therefore, the statement that the effect of genetic drift is more significant in large populations is incorrect.

Answer: The effect of genetic drift is more significant in large populations.

71833.subject: Chemistry
71833.text: What is the correct order of reactivity of haloalkanes towards $\beta$-elimination reaction?
71833.sol:
The reactivity of haloalkanes towards $\beta$-elimination reactions depends on the stability of the alkene formed as the product.

According to Saytzeff's rule, highly substituted alkenes are more stable due to a greater number of hyperconjugative structures.

Tertiary (3^{}^{\circ}$) haloalkanes yield more substituted alkenes compared to secondary (2^{}^{\circ}$) and primary (1^{}^{\circ}$) haloalkanes. Furthermore, the transition state in the elimination reaction is stabilized by the electron-donating inductive effect and hyperconjugation of the attached alkyl groups.

Therefore, the correct order of reactivity towards \beta$-elimination is $3^{}^{\circ} > 2^{}^{\circ} > 1^{}^{\circ}$.

Answer: $3^{}^{\circ} > 2^{}^{\circ} > 1^{}^{\circ}$

72549.text:
Directions: Identify which part of the given sentence contains a grammatical error.

When I saw Arnab he said he had taken his driving test yesterday.
72549.sol:
The error lies in part (3) of the given sentence.

The past perfect tense 'had taken' is incorrectly used with the definite past time adverb 'yesterday'. According to standard grammatical rules, the simple past tense should be used to describe an action that occurred at a specific time in the past indicated by words like 'yesterday', 'last week', or 'ago'.

Therefore, 'had taken his' should be replaced with 'took his' to make the sentence grammatically correct.

76468.text:
Consider the line $x=\sqrt{3} y$ and the circle $x^2+y^2=4$.
What is the area of the region in the first quadrant enclosed by the $x$-axis, the line $x=\sqrt{3} y$ and the circle?
76468.sol:
$\begin{aligned} & x^2+y^2=4 \text{ and } x=\sqrt{3} y \\ & P(\sqrt{3}, 1)=\text{ First quadrant }\end{aligned}$

The point of intersection of the line and the circle in the first quadrant is $(\sqrt{3}, 1)$.
Area of $\triangle \mathrm{OPA}=$ Area of $\triangle \mathrm{OPB}+$ Area of PAB
$=\frac{1}{2} \times \mathrm{OB} \times \mathrm{PB}=\frac{1}{2} \times \sqrt{3} \times 1=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\begin{aligned}
& \text{ Area of PAB } \int_{\sqrt{3}}^2 \mathrm{ydx} \\
& =\int_{\sqrt{3}}^2 \sqrt{4-x^2} d x=\left[\frac{x}{2} \sqrt{4-x^2}+\frac{4}{2} \sin ^{-1} \frac{x}{2}\right]_{\sqrt{3}}^2 \\
& {\left[2 \times \frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}[\sqrt{4-3}]-2 \sin ^{-1} \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right]} \\
& =\pi-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\frac{2 \pi}{3}=\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}
\end{aligned}$
Area enclosed by $x$-axis, the line $=\sqrt{3} . y$, and the circle $x^2+y^2=4$ in the first quadrant
$=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=\frac{\pi}{3}$

77248.text: If $x=k(\theta+\sin \theta)$ and $y=k(1+\cos \theta)$, then what is the derivative of $y$ with respect to $x$ at $\theta=\pi / 2$ ?
77248.sol: $\begin{aligned} x & =k(\theta+\sin \theta) \\ y & =k(1+\cos \theta) \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d x}{d \theta} & =k(1+\cos \theta) \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d \theta} & =k(0-\sin \theta) \\ \therefore \quad \frac{d y}{d x} & =\frac{-\sin \theta}{1+\cos \theta} \\ & =\frac{-\sin \frac{\pi}{2}}{1+\cos \frac{\pi}{2}} \\ & =\frac{-1}{1}=-1\end{aligned}$

77431.subject: Mathematics
77431.text: A plane is observed to be approaching the airport. It is at a distance of $10$ km from the point of observation and makes an angle of elevation of $67\cdot5^{}^{\circ}$. What is the height of the plane above the ground ?
77431.sol:
Let $h$ be the height of the plane above the ground.

The distance from the point of observation to the plane is $d = 10$ km.

The angle of elevation is $\theta = 67.5^{}^{\circ}$.

From the right-angled triangle formed, $\sin \theta = \dfrac{h}{d}$.

$h = 10 \sin 67.5^{}^{\circ}$

Using the half-angle formula, $\sin \theta = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - \cos 2\theta}{2}}$.

$\sin 67.5^{}^{\circ} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - \cos 135^{}^{\circ}}{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - \left(-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\sqrt{2} + 1}{2\sqrt{2}}}$

Multiplying the numerator and denominator inside the square root by $\sqrt{2}:

\sin 67.5^{}^{\circ} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 + \sqrt{2}}{4}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2}}}{2}$

Substituting this value into the equation for $h$:

$h = 10 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2}}}{2} = 5\sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2}}$ km

83004.subject: Physics
83004.text: At a point $A$ on the earth’s surface the angle of dip, $\delta = + 25 °$. At a point $B$ on the earth’s surface, the angle of dip, $\delta = - 25 °$. We can interpret that:
options: $A$ and $B$ are both located in the northern hemisphere.
$A$ is located in the southern hemisphere and $B$ is located in the northern hemisphere.
$A$ is located in the northern hemisphere and $B$ is located in the southern hemisphere.
$A$ and $B$ are both located in the southern hemisphere.
83004.sol:
As we know that the angle of dip is the angle between earth's resultant magnetic field from horizontal.

At the equator, dip is zero. At Northern Hemisphere, dip is positive. At Southern Hemisphere, dip is negative.

Since, the field lines originate from the South Pole, the angle of dip is negative in Southern Hemisphere. Similarly, as the field lines terminate at the North Pole, the angle of dip is positive in Northern Hemisphere.

83283.subject: Physics
83283.text:
The sum of kinetic energy and potential energy of a simple pendulum bob is $0.02$ joule. The speed of the simple pendulum bob at equilibrium position is approximately :
(Consider mass of the bob $= 20$ g)
83283.sol:
Total energy of the simple pendulum is given as $E = 0.02$ J.

Mass of the bob, $m = 20$ g $= 0.02$ kg.

At the equilibrium position, the potential energy is zero and the total energy is purely kinetic.

$E = \dfrac{1}{2} m v^2$

$0.02 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 0.02 \times v^2$

$v^2 = 2$

$v = \sqrt{2} \approx 1.41$ m/s.

Answer: $1.41$ m/s

85133.text: People living at sea level have around 5 million RBC per cubic millimeter of their blood whereas those living at an altitude to 5400 metres have around 8 million. This is because at high altitude:
options: people eat more nutritive food. therefore more RBCs are formed
people get pollution-free air to breathe and more oxygen is available
atmospheric $\mathrm{O}_2$ level is less and hence more RBCs are needed to absorb the required amount of $\mathrm{O}_2$ to survive.
there is more UV radiation which enhances RBC production
85133.sol:
As we move from low altitude to high altitude, the air starts getting thinner and thinner. The partial pressure of oxygen starts decreasing with increasing altitude. Now, since the partial pressure of oxygen is less in our lungs, the binding of oxygen to haemoglobin in RBCs also decreases. As a result, there is decreased oxygen supply to the tissues thereby starving them of oxygen. This situation leads to the release of the hormone erythropoietin from the kidneys, which stimulates the bone marrow to increase the production of RBCs.
Related Theory
Oxygen is carried in the blood in two forms: (i) dissolved in plasma and RBC water (about $2 \%$ of the total) and (ii) reversibly bound to haemoglobin (about $98 \%$ of the total). The haemoglobin molecule has four binding sites for oxygen molecules: the iron atoms in the four heme groups. Thus, each $\mathrm{Hb}$ tetramer can bind four oxygen molecules.

91868.text: If $\left({1}^{2} - {a}_{1}\right) + \left({2}^{2} - {a}_{2}\right) + \left({3}^{2} - {a}_{3}\right) + . \ldots \ldots . . + \left({n}^{2} - {a}_{n}\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}n\left({n}^{2} - 1\right),$ then the value of ${a}_{7}$ is
91868.sol:
$\left({1}^{2} + {2}^{2} + {3}^{3} + . \ldots \ldots + {n}^{2}\right) - \left({a}_{1} + {a}_{2} + {a}_{3} + . \ldots \ldots + {a}_{n}\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}n\left({n}^{2} - 1\right)$
Replace $n$ by $\left(n - 1\right)$
$\left({1}^{2} + {2}^{2} + {3}^{3} + . \ldots \ldots + {\left(n - 1\right)}^{2}\right) - \left({a}_{1} + {a}_{2} + {a}_{3} + . \ldots \ldots + {a}_{n - 1}\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(n - 1\right)\left({\left(n - 1\right)}^{2} - 1\right)$
Subtracting these two equations, we get,
${n}^{2} - {a}_{n} = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(n - 1\right)\left\{n\left(n + 1\right) - \left({n}^{2} + 1 - 2n - 1\right)\right\} = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(n - 1\right)\left\{{n}^{2} + n - {n}^{2} + 2n\right\}$
$= {n}^{2} - n$
$⇒ {a}_{n} = n ⇒ {a}_{7} = 7$

92726.text: The antenna current of an AM transmitter is $8A$ when only the carrier is sent, but it increases to $8. 93A$ when the carrier is modulated by a single sine wave. Find the percentage modulation.
options:
$60. 1 %$
&
92726.sol:
The power dissipated in any circuit is a function of the square of voltage across the circuit and the effective resistance of the circuit. Equation of AM wave reveals that it has three components of amplitude Clearly; power output must be distributed among these components.

Carrier power, ${P}_{c} = \dfrac{{\left({E}_{c} / \sqrt{2}\right)}^{2}}{R} = \dfrac{{E}_c^{2}}{2R}$

Total power of side bands,

${P}_{S} = \dfrac{{\left(m{E}_{c} / 2\sqrt{2}\right)}^{2}}{R} + \dfrac{{\left(m{E}_{c} / 2\sqrt{2}\right)}^{2}}{R} = \dfrac{m^{2}{E}_c^{2}}{4R}$

$∴ \dfrac{{P}_{S}}{{P}_{C}} = \dfrac{1}{2}m^{2}$

and ${P}_{T} = {P}_{C} + {P}_{S} = {P}_{C} \left(1 + \dfrac{m^{2}}{2}\right)

$∴ $\dfrac{{P}_{T}}{{P}_{C}} =1 + \dfrac{m^{2}}{2}$⇒ {$\left(\dfrac{{I}_{T}}{{I}_{C}}\right)$}^{2} = 1 + $\dfrac{m^{2}}{2}

Given that, ${I}_{T} = 8.93A, {I}_{C} = 8A, m = ?$

$∴ {$\left(\dfrac{8.93}{8}\right)$}^{2} = 1 + $\dfrac{m^{2}}{2}

Or 1.246 = 1 + \dfrac{m^{2}}{2}$ or$\dfrac{m^{2}}{2} =0.246$

Or $m = \sqrt{2 \times 0.246} =0.701 = 70.1%$

93778.sol:
Using the 3rd equation of motion

$V^{2} = u^{2} + 2gh$

${V}_{2} = \sqrt{{V}_{0}^{2} + 2gh}$

Using the equation of continuity

${A}_{1}{V}_{1} = {A}_{2}{V}_{2}$

we get $\dfrac{A2}{A1} = \dfrac{V0}{{V}_{0}^{2} + 2gh}$

Required condition $\dfrac{A1}{A2} = \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{V0}{{V}_{0}^{2} + 2gh}$

$⇒ 4{V}_{0}^{2} = {V}_{0}^{2} + 2gh$

$h = \dfrac{3{V}_{0}^{2}}{2g}$

96569.text: Which of the following constitutes of a micro-ecosystem?
96569.sol:
A community of organisms interacting with abiotic component in a particular region/area will be called as ecosystem. The living and non-living components are linked together by the nutrient cycles and energy flow through each trophic level.

Regions or locations defined by critical environmental factors within small spaces contain the micro-ecosystem. Pond is a classic example of microecosystem with limited water volume generally for short duration. These are generally colonized by organisms which are do not live in water continuously and by organisms possessing drought-resistant spores in their life cycle.

both organic and inorganic nutrients from detritus
96642.sol: Mineralization is the last step of decomposition, after humification, during which humus is formed. Humus is colloidal in nature which serves as a reservoir of inorganic nutrients. So, during mineralization inorganic nutrients are withdrawn with the help of microbes. At the level of detritus, fragmentation takes place due to which smaller particles are formed and during catabolism, detritus degrades into smaller inorganic substances with the help of bacterial and fungal enzymes.

97205.sol:
In arithmetic growth, the cell divides giving rise to two daughter cells. From which, only one daughter cell continues to divide while the other differentiates and matures to become a permanent cell. This kind of nature of growth rate is shown by meristematic cells.

Plasticity is the ability of the tissues to form different structures in response to environmental conditions. Senescence is the deterioration phase with respect to the ageing of a cell or tissue or an organism.

100224.text: A particle is moving unidirectional on a horizontal plane under the action of a constant power supplying energy source. The displacement (s) – time (t) graph that describes the motion of the particle is (graphs are drawn schematically and are not to scale):
100224.sol:
Here Power is constant,
Hence, $P = Fv = mav = av = constant .$

$av = k$
$v\dfrac{dv}{dx} \times v = k$
${∫}_{0}^{v}{v}^{2}dv = k{∫}_{0}^{x}dx$
$∴ v = {\left(3k\right)}^{1 / 3} \times {\left(x\right)}^{1 / 3} ⇒ v = A{\left(x\right)}^{1 / 3}whereA = {\left(3k\right)}^{1 / 3} = constant . . . . \left(1\right)$

Also, $v = \dfrac{dx}{dt}$$∴ \dfrac{dx}{dt} = A{\left(x\right)}^{1 / 3} ⇒ {∫}_{0}^{d}\dfrac{dx}{{\left(x\right)}^{1 / 3}} = A{∫}_{0}^{t}dt$

Simplifying further we get,

$⇒ d = A{\left(t\right)}^{3 / 2} . . . \left(2\right)$

From equations $\left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$ its clear that the graph won't be straight line so first & third options cant be correct.
Now, from equation $\left(1\right)$ its clear that when $x$ is increased then the slope $\dfrac{ds}{dt}$ should also increase which is possible in second option. Hence option $2$ is correct.

100355.subject: Physics
100355.text: A particle starts from rest and moves with uniform acceleration in a straight line. It covers the first half of its total distance with an average velocity $v_1$, and the second half of its total distance with an average velocity $v_2$. The ratio $\dfrac{v_2}{v_1}$ is equal to:
100355.sol:
Let the total distance be $2d$ and the uniform acceleration be $a$.

The velocity of the particle at the start is $u = 0$.
Using the third equation of motion, $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$, the velocity at the midpoint (distance $d$) is $v' = \sqrt{2ad}$.
The velocity at the end of the journey (distance $2d$) is $v'' = \sqrt{2a(2d)} = 2\sqrt{ad}$.

For uniformly accelerated motion, the average velocity over any interval is the arithmetic mean of the initial and final velocities for that interval.
Average velocity for the first half, $v_1 = \dfrac{0 + \sqrt{2ad}}{2}$.
Average velocity for the second half, $v_2 = \dfrac{\sqrt{2ad} + 2\sqrt{ad}}{2}$.

The ratio is:
$\dfrac{v_2}{v_1} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2ad} + 2\sqrt{ad}}{\sqrt{2ad}} = 1 + \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2} + 1$.

Answer: $\sqrt{2} + 1$

100496.subject: Physics
100496.text: A grasshopper leaps from the ground with an initial speed of $2\text{ m/s}$ at an angle of $60^{\circ}$ to the horizontal. The maximum vertical height cleared by the grasshopper during its leap is (take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
100496.sol:
Given: initial speed $u = 2\text{ m/s}$, angle of projection $\theta = 60^{\circ}$, and $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$.

The maximum height $H$ attained by a projectile is given by the formula:
$H = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2 \theta}{2g}$

Substitute the given values into the formula:
$\sin 60^{\circ} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$
$\sin^2 60^{\circ} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$H = \dfrac{(2)^2 \times \left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)}{2 \times 10}$
$H = \dfrac{4 \times \dfrac{3}{4}}{20}$
$H = \dfrac{3}{20}\text{ m}$

To convert the height into centimeters, multiply by $100$:
$H = \dfrac{3}{20} \times 100\text{ cm} = 15\text{ cm}$.

Answer: $15\text{ cm}$

100698.subject: Physics
100698.text: A block of mass $3 \mathrm{~kg}$ is placed on a frictionless inclined plane of angle $30^{\circ}$. It is connected to a hanging block of mass $2 \mathrm{~kg}$ by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth pulley at the top of the incline. When the system is released from rest, what is the acceleration of the blocks? (Take $g = 10 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-2}$)
100698.sol:
Let $a$ be the common acceleration of the system and $T$ be the tension in the string.

For the hanging block of mass $M = 2 \mathrm{~kg}$, the weight acts downwards ($M g = 20 \mathrm{~N}$).
For the block of mass $m = 3 \mathrm{~kg}$ on the incline, the component of weight acting down the incline is $m g \sin 30^{\circ} = 3(10)(0.5) = 15 \mathrm{~N}$.

Since $20 \mathrm{~N} > 15 \mathrm{~N}$, the $2 \mathrm{~kg}$ block will accelerate downwards and the $3 \mathrm{~kg}$ block will accelerate up the incline.

Writing the equations of motion for both blocks:
For the $2 \mathrm{~kg}$ block: $20 - T = 2a$
For the $3 \mathrm{~kg}$ block: $T - 15 = 3a$

Adding the two equations to eliminate $T$:
$(20 - T) + (T - 15) = 2a + 3a$
$5 = 5a$
$a = 1 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-2}$

Answer: $1 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-2}$

(IV) The graph of $PV$ versus $P$ at a constant temperature is a straight line passing through the origin.

How many of the above statements are correct?
102239.sol:
Statement I is correct: From the ideal gas equation $V = \left(\dfrac{nR}{P}\right)T$, the slope of a $V$-$T$ graph is $\dfrac{nR}{P}$. A steeper slope means a larger value of $\dfrac{nR}{P}$, which corresponds to a lower pressure.

Statement II is incorrect: From $P = \left(\dfrac{nR}{V}\right)T$, the slope of a $P$-$T$ graph is $\dfrac{nR}{V}$. A steeper slope means a larger value of $\dfrac{nR}{V}$, which corresponds to a lower volume, not higher.

Statement III is correct: In a $P$-$V$ graph, $PV = nRT$. For a higher temperature $T$, the product $PV$ is larger, so the rectangular hyperbola lies further from the origin.

Statement IV is incorrect: At constant temperature, Boyle's law states that $PV = \text{constant}$. Thus, the graph of $PV$ versus $P$ is a horizontal straight line parallel to the pressure axis, not passing through the origin.

Therefore, exactly two statements (I and III) are correct.

Answer: Only two

102657.subject: Physics
102657.text: An open organ pipe and a closed organ pipe, both of the same length $L$, are vibrating in their respective resonant modes. It is observed that the standing wave pattern in both the pipes contains exactly $4$ displacement nodes. The ratio of the frequency of the open pipe to the frequency of the closed pipe is :
102657.sol:
For an open organ pipe, the $p^{th}$ harmonic contains $p$ displacement nodes.

Since the open pipe has $4$ nodes, it is vibrating in its $4^{th}$ harmonic. Its frequency is $f_{open} = 4 \left(\dfrac{v}{2L}\right) = \dfrac{2v}{L}$.

For a closed organ pipe, only odd harmonics are present. The $q^{th}$ harmonic (where $q$ is an odd integer) contains $\dfrac{q+1}{2}$ displacement nodes.

Given that the closed pipe has $4$ nodes, we have $\dfrac{q+1}{2} = 4 \Rightarrow q = 7$. Thus, it is vibrating in its $7^{th}$ harmonic. Its frequency is $f_{closed} = 7 \left(\dfrac{v}{4L}\right) = \dfrac{7v}{4L}$.

The ratio of their frequencies is $\dfrac{f_{open}}{f_{closed}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{2v}{L}}{\dfrac{7v}{4L}} = \dfrac{8}{7}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{8}{7}$

103353.subject: Physics
103353.text: In a meter bridge experiment with a $100\text{ cm}$ long uniform wire, an unknown resistance $X$ is connected in the left gap and a known resistance of $10\ \Omega$ is connected in the right gap. If the galvanometer shows a null deflection when the jockey is placed at a distance of $25\text{ cm}$ from the right end of the bridge wire, the value of the unknown resistance $X$ is:
103353.sol:
In a meter bridge, the balancing condition is given by $\dfrac{R_1}{l_1} = \dfrac{R_2}{l_2}$, where $l_1$ and $l_2$ are the balancing lengths from the left and right ends respectively.

Given that the balance point is at $25\text{ cm}$ from the right end, we have $l_2 = 25\text{ cm}$.

The length from the left end is $l_1 = 100 - 25 = 75\text{ cm}$.

The resistance in the right gap is $R_2 = 10\ \Omega$.

Let the unknown resistance in the left gap be $X$. Applying the balancing condition:
$\dfrac{X}{75} = \dfrac{10}{25}$

$X = 75 \times \dfrac{10}{25} = 3 \times 10 = 30\ \Omega$

Answer: $30\ \Omega$

103694.subject: Physics
103694.text:
A circular coil of $50$ turns and radius $10$ cm has a magnetic moment of $3.14$ A m$^2$. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre of the coil?
(Take $\pi = 3.14$ and $\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}$ T m/A)
103694.sol:
The magnetic moment of a circular coil is given by:

$M = N I A = N I \pi R^2$

Given $M = 3.14$ A m$^2$ and taking $\pi = 3.14$, we can write $M = \pi$ A m$^2$.

Substituting the given values ($N = 50$, $R = 0.1$ m):

$\pi = 50 \times I \times \pi \times (0.1)^2$

$1 = 50 \times I \times 0.01$

$1 = 0.5 I \implies I = 2$ A

The magnetic field at the centre of the coil is:

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 N I}{2R}$

$B = \dfrac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 50 \times 2}{2 \times 0.1}$

$B = \dfrac{400\pi \times 10^{-7}}{0.2}$

$B = 2000\pi \times 10^{-7} = 2\pi \times 10^{-4}$ T

Alternatively, substituting $NI = \dfrac{M}{\pi R^2}$ directly into the magnetic field formula yields:

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 M}{2\pi R^3} = \dfrac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times \pi}{2\pi \times (0.1)^3} = 2\pi \times 10^{-4}$ T

Answer: $2\pi \times 10^{-4}$ T

104194.subject: Physics
104194.text: A choke is preferred to a resistance for limiting current in AC circuit because
options: there is no wastage of power
choke is a good absorber of heat
104194.sol:
In an AC circuit, the coil of high inductance and negligible resistance used to control current, is called the choke coil. The power factor of such a coil is given by
$\cos \phi=\frac{R}{\sqrt{R^2+\omega^2 L^2}}$
$=\frac{R}{\omega L} \quad($ as $R \ll \lt \omega L)$
As $R \ll \omega L, \cos \phi$ is very small. Thus, the power absorbed by the coil is very small. The only loss of energy is due to hysteresis in the iron core, which is much less than the loss of energy in the resistance that can also reduce the current if placed instead of the choke coil.

105570.subject: Physics
105570.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When the frequency of incident light on a photosensitive surface is doubled, the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons becomes more than double.

Reason (R): The maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons is directly proportional to the frequency of incident light.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
105570.sol:
Let the initial frequency of incident light be $ u$ and the work function of the surface be $\Phi$.
According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, the initial maximum kinetic energy is:
$K_1 = h u - \Phi$

When the frequency is doubled ($2 u$), the new maximum kinetic energy is:
$K_2 = h(2 u) - \Phi = 2h u - \Phi$

We can rewrite $K_2$ in terms of $K_1$:
$K_2 = 2(K_1 + \Phi) - \Phi = 2K_1 + \Phi$

Since the work function $\Phi$ is a positive quantity, $K_2 > 2K_1$. Therefore, the maximum kinetic energy becomes more than double. Thus, Assertion (A) is correct.

The equation $K_{\max} = h u - \Phi$ represents a linear relationship between maximum kinetic energy and frequency, but it is not a direct proportionality because the graph does not pass through the origin (due to the non-zero intercept $-\Phi$). Thus, Reason (R) is incorrect.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

113896.subject: Chemistry
113896.text: Which of the following aqueous solutions will have the highest freezing point? (Assume complete dissociation for strong electrolytes)
113896.sol:
Depression in freezing point is given by $\Delta T_f = i \times K_f \times m$.

Assuming molality is approximately equal to molarity for dilute solutions, $\Delta T_f \propto i \times M$.
The freezing point of the solution is $T_f = T_f^\circ - \Delta T_f$. To have the highest freezing point, the solution must exhibit the minimum depression in freezing point ($\Delta T_f$), which corresponds to the lowest effective concentration ($i \times M$).

Calculating $i \times M$ for each given solution:
1. 0.15 M $\mathrm{NaCl}$: $i = 2$ ($\mathrm{Na}^+, \mathrm{Cl}^-$), so $i \times M = 2 \times 0.15 = 0.30$
2. 0.2 M Urea: $i = 1$ (non-electrolyte), so $i \times M = 1 \times 0.2 = 0.20$
3. 0.05 M $\mathrm{Al}_2(\mathrm{SO}_4)_3$: $i = 5$ ($2\mathrm{Al}^{3+}, 3\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}$), so $i \times M = 5 \times 0.05 = 0.25$
4. 0.1 M $\mathrm{BaCl}_2$: $i = 3$ ($\mathrm{Ba}^{2+}, 2\mathrm{Cl}^-$), so $i \times M = 3 \times 0.1 = 0.30$

Since 0.2 M Urea has the lowest $i \times M$ value (0.20), it will have the minimum depression in freezing point and therefore the highest freezing point.

Answer: 0.2 M Urea

114358.subject: Chemistry
114358.text: A conductivity cell is filled with a $0.01\text{ M}$ solution of a weak acid. The resistance of the solution is $2500\text{ }\Omega$ and the cell constant is $0.5\text{ cm}^{-1}$. If the limiting molar conductivity of the weak acid is $400\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$, what is its degree of dissociation?
114358.sol:
First, calculate the conductivity ($\kappa$) of the solution using the cell constant ($G^*$) and resistance ($R$):

$\kappa = \dfrac{G^*}{R} = \dfrac{0.5}{2500} = 2 \times 10^{-4}\text{ S cm}^{-1}$

Next, calculate the molar conductivity ($\Lambda_m$) of the solution:

$\Lambda_m = \dfrac{\kappa \times 1000}{c} = \dfrac{2 \times 10^{-4} \times 1000}{0.01} = \dfrac{0.2}{0.01} = 20\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$

Finally, calculate the degree of dissociation ($\alpha$):

$\alpha = \dfrac{\Lambda_m}{\Lambda_m^\circ} = \dfrac{20}{400} = 0.05$

Answer: $0.05$

116354.subject: Chemistry
116354.text:
Match the species in List-I with their characteristic bonding features in List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) $\text{N}_2$(I) $p\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bond
(B) $\text{R}_3\text{P}=\text{CH}_2$(II) $d\pi$-$p\pi$ bond
(C) $\text{PR}_3$ complex with transition metals(III) $d\pi$-$d\pi$ bond
(D) $\text{P}_4$(IV) Only single bonds

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
116354.sol:
Nitrogen lacks d-orbitals in its valence shell and its small size allows it to form strong $p\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bonds. Thus, $\text{N}_2$ exists as a diatomic molecule with a triple bond.

Heavier elements like phosphorus have vacant d-orbitals. In compounds like $\text{R}_3\text{P}=\text{CH}_2$, phosphorus utilizes its d-orbitals to form a $d\pi$-$p\pi$ bond with carbon.

Phosphorus can also act as a $\pi$-acceptor ligand, forming $d\pi$-$d\pi$ back-bonds with the filled d-orbitals of transition metals in $\text{PR}_3$ complexes.

Due to their larger size and diffuse orbitals, heavier Group 15 elements do not form stable $p\pi$-$p\pi$ bonds. Consequently, phosphorus exists as a discrete tetrahedral $\text{P}_4$ molecule containing only single $\text{P}-\text{P}$ bonds.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)

121784.subject: Botany
121784.text: How do mosses contribute to soil formation?
121784.sol: Bryophytes in general are of little economic importance but some mosses provide food for herbaceous mammals, birds and other animals. Species of Sphagnum, a moss, provide peat that have long been used as fuel, and as packing material for trans-shipment of living material because of their capacity to hold water. Mosses along with lichens are the first organisms to colonize rocks and hence, are of great ecological importance. <mark>They decompose rocks making the substrate suitable for the growth of higher plants.</mark> Since moses form dense mats on the soil, they reduce the impact of falling rain and prevent soil erosion. The bryophytes are divided into liverworts and mosses.Zygote thereafter produces a multicellular well-differentiated sporophyte which is the dominant phase of the pteridophytes. In the majority of the pteridophytes all the spores are of similar kinds; such plants are called homosporous. Genera like Selaginella and Salvinia which produce two kinds of spores, macro (large) and micro (small) spores, are known as heterosporous. The megaspores and microspores germinate and give rise to female and male gametophytes, respectively. The female gametophytes in these plants are retained on the parent sporophytes for variable periods.
121784.meta: How do mosses contribute to soil formation?

121816.subject: Botany
121816.text: What process occurs in the spore mother cells within the sporangia?
121816.sol: The Pteridophytes include horsetails and ferns. Pteridophytes are used for medicinal purposes and as soil-binders. They are also frequently grown as ornamentals. Evolutionarily, they are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues – xylem and phloem. The pteridophytes are found in cool, damp, shady places though some may flourish well in sandy-soil conditions. In pteridophytes, the main plant body is a sporophyte which is differentiated into true root, stem and leaves (Figure 3.3). These organs possess well-differentiated vascular tissues. The leaves in pteridophytes are small (microphylls) as in Selaginella or large (macrophylls) as in ferns. The sporophytes bear sporangia that are subtended by leaf-like appendages called sporophylls. In some cases sporophylls may form distinct compact structures called strobili or cones (Selaginella, Equisetum). <mark>The sporangia produce spores by meiosis in spore mother cells.</mark>

123643.text: In which organism does mitosis lead to the formation of syncytium?
123643.sol: Plant cells however, are enclosed by a relatively inextensible cell wall, thererfore they undergo cytokinesis by a different mechanism. In plant cells, wall formation starts in the centre of the cell and grows outward to meet the existing lateral walls. The formation of the new cell wall begins with the formation of a simple precursor, called the cell-plate that represents the middle lamella between the walls of two adjacent cells. At the time of cytoplasmic division, organelles like mitochondria and plastids get distributed between the two daughter cells. In some organisms, karyokinesis is not followed by cytokinesis as a result of which multinucleate condition arises leading to the formation of syncytium (e.g., liquid endosperm in coconut).

127993.subject: Zoology
127993.text: What is the cloaca used for in frogs?
options: Passing faecal matter, urine, and sperms
Passing faecal matter and urine only
127993.sol: Frogs have well organised male and female reproductive systems. Male reproductive organs consist of a pair of yellowish ovoid testes , which are found adhered to the upper part of kidneys by a double fold of peritoneum called mesorchium. Vasa efferentia are 10-12 in number that arise from testes. They enter the kidneys on their side and open into Bidder’s canal. Finally it communicates with the urinogenital duct that comes out of the kidneys and opens into the cloaca. The cloaca is a small, median chamber that is used to pass faecal matter, urine and sperms to the exterior. The female reproductive organs include a pair of ovaries The ovaries are situated near kidneys and there is no functional connection with kidneys. A pair of oviduct arising from the ovaries opens into the cloaca separately. A mature female can lay 2500 to 3000 ova at a time. Fertilisation is external and takes place in water. Development involves a larval stage called tadpole. Tadpole undergoes metamorphosis to form the adult.Frogs are beneficial for mankind because they eat insects and protect the crop. Frogs maintain ecological balance because these serve as an important link of food chain and food web in the ecosystem. In some countries the muscular legs of frog are used as food by man.

129351.subject: Zoology
129351.text: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is present in the subarachnoid space of the human central neural system. Based on the anatomical sequence of the cranial meninges, this space is located between which of the following two layers?
129351.sol:
The cranial meninges consist of three layers: the outer dura mater, the middle arachnoid, and the inner pia mater.

The term "subarachnoid" indicates a position beneath the arachnoid layer. Therefore, the subarachnoid space lies between the middle layer (arachnoid) and the innermost layer (pia mater).

The space between the dura mater and arachnoid is the subdural space, while the space between the cranium (skull) and dura mater is the epidural space.

Answer: Arachnoid and Pia mater

129581.subject: Zoology
129581.text: What is added to the blood drained from an artery during hemodialysis?
129581.sol: Malfunctioning of kidneys can lead to accumulation of urea in blood, a condition called uremia, which is highly harmful and may lead to kidney failure. In such patients, urea can be removed by a process called hemodialysis. During the process of haemodialysis, the blood drained from a convenient artery is pumped into a dialysing unit called artificial kidney.. Blood drained from a convenient artery is pumped into a dialysing unit after adding an anticoagulant like heparin. The unit contains a coiled cellophane tube surrounded by a fluid (dialysing fluid) having the same composition as that of plasma except the nitrogenous wastes. The porous cellophane membrance of the tube allows the passage of molecules based on concentration gradient. As nitrogenous wastes are absent in the dialysing fluid, these substances freely move out, thereby clearing the blood. The cleared blood is pumped back to the body through a vein after adding anti-heparin to it. This method is a boon for thousands of uremic patients all over the world.

129921.subject: Zoology
129921.text: What is the role of oxygen in the respiration process?
options: To create pressure gradients between the atmosphere and the alveoli
To estimate air volume in inspiration and expiration
129921.sol: Oxygen provides energy to cells during respiration. As you have read earlier, oxygen (O2) is utilised by the organisms to indirectly break down simple molecules like glucose, amino acids, fatty acids, etc., to derive energy to perform various activities. Carbon dioxide (CO2) which is harmful is also released during the above catabolic reactions. It is, therefore, evident that O2 has to be continuously provided to the cells and CO2 produced by the cells have to be released out. This process of exchange of O2 from the atmosphere with CO2 produced by the cells is called breathing, commonly known as respiration. Place your hands on your chest; you can feel the chest moving up and down. You know that it is due to breathing. How do we breathe? The respiratory organs and the mechanism of breathing are described in the following sections of this chapter.

130471.text: The flat skull bones fuse end-to-end to form the cranium, creating a joint that does not allow any movement. Identify the category of this joint and the specific tissue involved in its formation.
options: Synovial joint; dense regular connective tissue
Fibrous joint; dense fibrous connective tissues
130471.sol:
According to NCERT, fibrous joints do not allow any movement. This type of joint is shown by the flat skull bones which fuse end-to-end with the help of dense fibrous connective tissues in the form of sutures, to form the cranium.

Cartilaginous joints involve cartilages and permit limited movement. Synovial joints are characterised by the presence of a fluid-filled synovial cavity between the articulating surfaces of the two bones and allow considerable movement. Loose connective tissue is not the structural component of sutures.

Answer: Fibrous joint; dense fibrous connective tissues

131856.subject: Zoology
131856.text:
Consider the following double-stranded DNA sequence of a transcription unit:

Strand I: 5' - A T G C A T G - 3'
Strand II: 3' - T A C G T A C - 5'

If the promoter is located towards the 5' end of Strand I, what will be the sequence of the transcribed mRNA?
options: 5' - C A U G C A U - 3'
3' - U A C G U A C - 5'
5' - A T G C A T G - 3'
5' - A U G C A U G - 3'
131856.sol:
According to the conventions for defining a transcription unit, the promoter is located towards the 5' end of the coding strand.

Since the promoter is located at the 5' end of Strand I, Strand I is the coding strand and Strand II is the template strand.

The mRNA is transcribed from the template strand (Strand II) and has a sequence complementary to it, which makes it identical to the coding strand (Strand I), except that thymine (T) is replaced by uracil (U).

Coding strand (Strand I): 5' - A T G C A T G - 3'
Transcribed mRNA: 5' - A U G C A U G - 3'

Answer: 5' - A U G C A U G - 3'

132532.subject: Zoology
132532.text: Which of the following disorders are caused due to recessive autosomal mutations?
options: Turner's syndrome and sickle cell anaemia
132532.sol:
Cystic fibrosis is an abnormal recessive disorder of infants, children and young adults that is due to an abnormal recessive autosomal allele present on chromosome 7 . In $70 \%$ of cases, it is due to deletion of three bases. The disease gets its name from the fibrous cysts that appear in the pancreas. It produces a defective glycoprotein. The defective glycoprotein causes formation of thick mucus in skin, lungs, pancreas, liver and other secretory organs. There is maldigestion of food with high fat content in stool. Liver may undergo cirrhosis. Phenylketonuria is an inborn, autosomal, recessive metabolic disorder in which the homozygous recessive individual lacks the enzyme phenylalanine hydroxylase needed to change phenylalanine to tyrosine in liver. It results in hyperphenylalaninemia which is characterised by accumulation and excretion of phenylalanine, phenylpyruvic acid and related compounds. Lack of the enzyme is due to the abnormal autosomal recessive gene chromosome 12 .
$\times 0$
